subject: distsamp sampling and effective sampling area variability

messages.author: e5841ce9d01eda50
messages.subject: distsamp sampling and effective sampling area variability
parts:
I am using count data as my dependent variable, and individual transects are my sampling unit, however my transects have variable effective sampling areas.

I have two very distinct vegetation types for the data, open and closed, which significantly impacts the detection of wildlife.
Prior to using 'unmarked' I determined the effective strip width (ESW) of each vegetation class, and then by controlling for the proportion of each vegetation class along each transect, I determined the effective sample area of each transect.
How do I take this into account in 'unmarked' thought? Should I create an offset term of my effective sampling area?

Perhaps I am thinking about this wrong though and because the model is hierarchical it is taking detection into account already, and thus is it not good to determine ESW beforehand?
If so, then how/where can this be included?
What I have is wildlife count per transect, but each transect has a count of wildlife in open vegetation and a count of wildlife in closed vegetation, and the length of each transect in each vegetation class is different along each transect. Hence my problem!

distsamp requires a transect level format, which is why I thought creating an offset term for each transect would be good. But if not, I have read that the function ForestDistData can be used to convert my individual-level distance data to the transect-level format. Is there somewhere here, or in another function where the individual-level location (open vs. closed) can be taken into account?

I hope this makes sense. Many thanks for any advice!

messages.author: 02d195331194f5bd
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] distsamp sampling and effective sampling area variability
parts:
I would recommend treating the two habitat types as distinct transects. Then you can include habitat type as a covariate of detection and/or abundance. 

Alternatively, if there are other covariates at the transect level that you really don't want to pseudoreplicate, you could keep the transects the same and include the proportion of open habitat as a covariate. 

On second thought, it might be best just to analyze it both ways and ensure that they give similar answers.

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] distsamp sampling and effective sampling area variability
parts:
hello,

  If you have observations of individuals along the transect and record their spatial location then you can use the pixel frequency model which is in unmarked to accommodate within-transect heterogeneity in habitat.  This is called pcount.spHDS -- that is the only way to do it in unmarked, but it is also possible to do this in JAGS or other Bayesian analysis packages. We have an example for point count data in the AHM book and AHM volume 2 has an example of this with transects.  A related paper is Mizel et al. (2018):
Mizel, J.D., Schmidt, J.H. and Lindberg, M.S., 2018. Accommodating temporary emigration in spatial distance sampling models. Journal of applied ecology, 55(3), pp.1456-1464.

 AHM v2 is not out yet but I'd be glad to send you a draft of that chapter off list.

 What Phil said also could be reasonable if the covariates are more like transect level covariates and not within-transect covariates.

regards
andy

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] distsamp sampling and effective sampling area variability
parts:
Thank you for your replies.

Unfortunately, besides the possible issue of pseudo-replication, I cannot divide my transects by vegetation type because the habitat type switches back and forth along the transect, which would make it difficult to link my covariates.
Also, I do plan to add proportion of closed vegetation (or % forest cover) as a covariate, however, this is at the transect level rather than the observation-level and doesn't really get out the level of definition I am hoping to apply to detection.

Therefore, it sounds like what Andy is describing may be a more suitable option as it can deal with within transect heterogeneity. I'm not fully understanding pcount.spHDS though. Do you need to have repeated samples for this? I only sampled each location once. 
Also, it says it needs deals with raster covariates, which most of mine are, however I would also like to include covariates like food diversity and basal area which are not at the pixel level. This data was collected in plots along each transect.

I definitely think it would be helpful to take a look at the example of pcount.spHDS from transect data from the AHM vol 2 if you are willing to share it Andy. I would be very grateful!!

Thanks,
Adrienne

Hello all,

In reading about pcount.spHDS, the issue it poses for my analysis is that I can only enter continuous (raster) covariates, which means I'd have to exclude covariates that I think are important.  

I'd still like to find a way to use distsamp, or something equivalent (perhaps in another package).
I read in a previous post of Andy's that for unmarked you can use the fuction {formatDistData} to convert observations into transect level data, which seems approppriate for me except that it is noted that "there is no \code{obsCovs} argument, meaning that
distance-interval-level covariates cannot be included in the anlysis"
This is exactly what I need though! So, is there another function for including observation covariates?

Additionally, when compiling the metatdata for the transects, in regards to transect length, rather than saying something like e.g. tlength=rep(100, 7), is it possible to insert a matrix into the argument? Whereby there is a column for transect name and a column for transect length?

Thanks!
